$comment: Card styles of the Catacomb Etching set (Commander Vault capsule machine), written by art/machine-specs.mjs from career/machines/commander-vault.json: edit that file and re-run, not this one.
style: Dramatic chiaroscuro etching and charcoal wash: deep plum-black shadows, silvery bone highlights, cross-hatched stonework, single cold candlelit focal point.
rules: These are full-art pictures for playing cards: the client draws a small name plate over the top edge, mana symbols at the top right and power and toughness at the bottom right, so keep the main subject in the middle of the panel and the top 15% and bottom 15% calm and uncluttered (sky, ground, water, background texture), with nothing important in the corners. Each panel shows its own subject as one clear, readable scene, the same style and palette as its neighbours, as if the whole row were a matched, limited-edition art series.
spare: an extra painting in the same style: a pale armoured hand rising out of cracked crypt flagstones as silver smoke curls upward from a candle flame

items.subject: a pale armoured hand rising out of cracked crypt flagstones as silver smoke curls upward from a candle flame
fine luminous threads pulling a shrouded knight upright from a sunken marble sarcophagus
three hooded figures gathered around a brazier whose violet-black flame stretches high into a vaulted chamber
a towering horned shadow leaning over a candlelit lectern, turning a single heavy page for a small cloaked scholar
a sunken circular pit ringed with iron arches and bone pillars under a stark overhead shaft of cold light

the BACK of a playing card in the same style: a symmetrical ornamental design (it is seen upside down too) with a central emblem drawn from this set's theme, framed by a painted border; no logo, no oval, no five dots, no lettering
